answer: A stake-bonded identity market resists Sybils the way a karst cave resists flooding: each agent must lock a refundable deposit that only unlocks after verified work, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real capital. Like a relic preserved in an ocean of copies, the bond stays scarce while copies are cheap. An attacker who floods the network burns their own stake with every fake, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
